description: Noise and drone voice in which a slow square-wave modulator frequency- or amplitude-modulates an audio-rate square oscillator, mixed with white noise, with a sample and hold and an envelope of its own

params.text: Sets the rate of the modulator, 1Hz up to about 261.63Hz
Sets the pitch of the audio oscillator, from about 16.35Hz to about 2637Hz
Sends the modulator into the audio oscillator's frequency while it is lit; it can be lit alongside AM
Sends the modulator into the audio oscillator's level while it is lit; it can be lit alongside FM
Sets how strongly the modulator acts on the audio oscillator, 0% to 100%
Divides the modulator's rate down against the audio oscillator, 0% to 100%
Sets how much of the internal white noise is mixed into the output, 0% to 100%
Puts out clean white noise while it is lit, with the pitch, FM, AM and divider settings set aside; the panel marks it solo
Sets how long the envelope takes to rise, 1ms to 15 seconds
Sets how long the envelope takes to fall once the gate closes, 1ms to 15 seconds
Holds the envelope open for as long as it is lit, whatever the gate input is doing

inputs.text: Opens the envelope while it is high, and is ignored while Hold is lit or a cable is patched to the envelope input
Sets the pitch of the audio oscillator, 1V per octave added to the pitch knob
A rising edge takes a new sample of whatever is at the sample and hold input
The signal the sample and hold takes its samples from; with nothing patched it samples the internal noise
Replaces the envelope entirely while a cable is patched here, along with the gate input and the Hold button; 0-10V, so another module's envelope output drives this one
Adds to the modulation depth knob, 0-10V covering its whole travel, and each channel drives its own modulator
Adds to the divider knob, 0-10V covering its whole travel, and each channel drives its own modulator

outputs.text: The modulator on its own, running whether or not the envelope is open
The oscillator and noise mix with the envelope applied to its level
The envelope currently shaping the audio output, 0-10V
The voltage held since the last rising edge at the sample and hold clock

notes: the sample and hold section keeps a channel count of its own, taken from its clock and signal jacks, so it is independent of the rest of the panel.
the noise source is one generator shared by every polyphonic channel rather than one per channel, which follows the hardware.
the blue lamp flashes on each new sample and its brightness follows the size of the value held on channel 1.
